title: Swamp of Sorrows
body: The Swamp of Sorrows was once the northern reach of the Black Morass, whose southern half became barren waste when the Dark Portal was destroyed; what remained was named for those who died in the Second War. Long ago the Atal'ai trolls raised a temple here to their blood god Hakkar, until the green dragonflight drowned it beneath the Pool of Tears. Now the orcs of Stonard hold the south, Alliance caravans struggle toward Nethergarde Keep, and Broken exiles shelter at the Harborage from their own maddened kin.

title: The Harborage
body: In the north of the swamp a cluster of leather huts hung with crystals makes up the Harborage, refuge of the Broken who kept their minds after crossing from Draenor. The Lost Ones of the Fallow Sanctuary, once their own brethren, kill any who wander near and have stolen the sacred draenethyst. The village keeps careful terms with nearby Stonard, for its leader Magtoor believes the Horde would crush his people if they failed to honor it.

parts.body: Since the draenei joined the Alliance, the Harborage has drawn new attention: Anchorite Avuun has come to study the Lost Ones in hope of a cure, though it troubles him that the village deals with the Horde at all.

title: Stonard
body: Stonard is one of the oldest orc settlements in Azeroth, first raised by the old Horde in the Black Morass after the Dark Portal opened, and re-established by the new Horde. Its great hall is guarded by two burrows. From here Dispatch Commander Ruag relays the orders of Orgrimmar, wayfinders set out to chart the unmapped swamp, and Fel'zerul studies the sunken temple at the Warchief's command, hoping the Atal'ai's forbidden magic might serve the Horde.

parts.body: Since the blood elves joined the Horde, Stonard has a guest from Quel'Thalas: the warlock Cersei Dusksinger, who scorns the orcs for sitting idle so close to so much power and perfects a curse meant for the draenei.

title: Pool of Tears
body: The Pool of Tears is the great lake on the eastern side of the swamp, and beneath its dark water lies the Temple of Atal'Hakkar. The Atal'ai trolls built it to call their blood god Hakkar into the world, and the green dragonflight sank it to stop them. Atal'ai ruins still lie along the shore and under the water, cursed trolls haunt the stones, and green dragonkin stand guard, among them the ancient drake Somnus.

parts.body: An Atal'ai priest exiled to the Hinterlands told of Jammal'an the Prophet, who believes Hakkar's return will make his tribe immortal, and of the enchanted fetishes that might yet summon the god.

title: Itharius
body: Itharius dwells in a cave on the western edge of the swamp, an elf to all appearances, sharing it with a brood of green whelps that snap at anyone who intrudes. He greets strangers as if he has been expecting them: fate, he says, has brought them for a reason he takes no pleasure in. Many choices lie ahead of them, and he insists that there are correct ones.

parts.body: Itharius is no elf. He is of Ysera's green dragonflight, and his brother Eranikus, charged with watching the sunken temple, fell unwittingly to the corruption of the god the Atal'ai called forth and now lies trapped in a nightmare within the Dream.

title: Fallen Hero of the Horde
body: Beside the southern road toward the Blasted Lands stands the ghost of the orc who commanded Thrall's Grasp, twenty of the Warchief's finest soldiers. He made camp here on the border to await orders from Orgrimmar, but weeks passed without word, and young, ambitious and afraid of nothing, he led his men into the Blasted Lands. He has regretted it ever since, and his spirit lingers where he made that choice, seeking anyone willing to help him regain his honor.

parts.body: The orders had been sent after all, but murlocs ambushed the messengers and the Swamp Talker carried them off. Had he waited, nineteen of his men could have been spared.
sources: npc_text 1391 (greeting before any quest), 1392 and 1411 (shown while on quest 2784), 1451-1454 (shown while on quest 2801)

parts.body: He fled the forces that overwhelmed his men, came back to rescue them and was tortured to death. The demon lord Razelikh had torn out their souls and bound them to stones near the Dark Portal and among his servants.
sources: npc_text 1391 (greeting before any quest), 1392 and 1411 (shown while on quest 2784), 1451-1454 (shown while on quest 2801)

parts.body: The stones were shattered and his men set free. Each soul spoke a few last words as it broke loose, and of their commander, Trebor, they said it had not been his fault.
